timecoded_text_to_speech.text: I'm Haley Hargess and we are in the Media Center at L.E. County
High School and I'm here with Congressman Nick Ray Hall.
So tell me a little bit about why you're here.
Well this is to announce water to a section of Lincoln County that has been fighting for
decades to get clean, potable water.
And this money comes through a program that I was able to get through the Congress and
the monies to back it up that will provide this clean drinking water.
It's unfortunate but there are still many parts of this country that some in Washington
don't realize just don't have clean drinking water.
They take it as an automatic in the big cities but we often have to fight for it in the
rural parts of this country when it should not be that way.
So this funding goes toward providing water for Lincoln County.
We're now about 70% of the way of providing clean drinking water to the entire county.
So we have more to do and we'll continue fighting to do that.
So today's ceremony is to recognize those residents that have fought so long and hard
for clean water.
So this will definitely benefit Lincoln County?
Yes it will.
Yes it will and it should help property values to go up, should help insurance rates go
down.
It should make it more attractive for new small businesses to come into the area and
it's all part of the future to make sure that we have a place here where our children
and our grandchildren want to stay.
Well thank you.
Glad we could have you.
Good to be here.
Good to be here in Lincoln County.
That's cool.
